chapter_seo_title: Chapter 277: Ghost Comes – Li Huowang Battles a Mass Hysteria Monster
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang tries to stop a town-wide panic over a ghost that steals men’s manhood—but the lie has teeth.
og_title: Ghost Comes – Li Huowang vs The Koro Panic
og_description: A town gripped by mass hysteria meets a monster that feeds on their fear. Li Huowang must kill the lie—and then maintain it.
twitter_title: When a folk panic becomes real: Li Huowang’s worst battle yet
twitter_description: The “shrinking ghost” rumor turns murderous. Great chapter for new readers.

lore_anchors.definition: A face-covering made of threaded old Chinese coins; in folk Daoism, coins carry yang energy and can ward off malevolent spirits.
A written charm empowered by a cultivator’s spiritual energy; often used to seal or immobilize ghosts in xianxia fiction.
A local government office in imperial China, serving both administrative and judicial functions.
A fictional county in the Dao-Twisted World; its name roughly translates to “Skid County” or “Poor County,” hinting at its desperation.
A named blade in Li Huowang’s possession; a military-grade weapon said to be effective against both men and spirits.
A shamanic practitioner from Chinese folk religion who performs exorcisms and communicates with spirits; in the Dao-Twisted World, often corrupted or faked.

cultural_notes_faq.a: Yes, it is a documented culture-bound mass delusion known as Koro syndrome, with recorded outbreaks in China and Southeast Asia, including a major panic in Hainan in 1984-85.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why didn’t Li Huowang’s sword cut the ghost?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The ghost was not a conventional yin spirit; it was an entity with a physical, reinforced body that required a specific sealing ritual (a talisman) rather than brute force.
